accepted.reason: Observation-target alignment is good: hospitalization admissions plausibly lag infection, and delayed_I is explicitly recommended. SEIR adds only one latent stage (E) to help represent sharp, high-peaked dynamics without introducing an explicit H compartment that may be weakly identifiable in a 31-week single-season window. Fixed 1-week delay is a reasonable parsimonious default given the semantics note.

Also aligned with recommended delayed_I mapping and keeps structure parsimonious (SEIR). A 2-week delay is plausible for admissions in some settings and may better match peak timing if the series exhibits a longer lag; however, it increases risk of peak misalignment and compensatory parameter distortion relative to a 1-week delay, so it is lower priority than proposal 0.

rejected.reason: Although H matches the target label mechanistically, introducing an explicit H compartment (SEIHR) in a short single-season series raises identifiability risk for I→H and H outflow rates, especially with high peakiness where multiple parameter combinations can fit peak height/width. Surveillance note explicitly flags H as potentially weakly identifiable here, making delayed_I preferable.

SEIHR plus an I+H observation map is poorly aligned to the stated target semantics (hospitalization_rate) and risks conflating distinct processes (infection prevalence proxy vs admissions/occupancy). It adds complexity (explicit H) while also weakening interpretability/identifiability of the observation mapping in a short series.

SEIRS adds waning immunity, which is unlikely to be identifiable over 31 training weeks in a single season and can induce spurious dynamics (e.g., secondary bumps) that mimic noise/peak asymmetry. Given the high peakiness, this extra degree of freedom is more likely overfitting than justified fractional/memory-like behavior; delayed_I can be handled without adding S↔R cycling.

suggested_edits.edit: Clarify that the 2-week delay is intended to represent admissions lag (not reporting backlog) and note that it should be treated as a sensitivity alternative to the 1-week delay due to peak-timing misalignment risk in single-season data.

If retained for consideration, simplify observation alignment by allowing a delayed_I map instead of direct H, or explicitly justify why H is identifiable in this series (e.g., external constraints on hospitalization duration). Otherwise, keep SEIHR as a lower-priority template for longer/multi-season series.

If waning immunity is conceptually desired, constrain the rationale to multi-season contexts; for this single-season window, reframe as SEIR with delayed_I rather than SEIRS to reduce over-complexity and identifiability risk.
